newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end up, lose ground in bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares end up, lose ground in bourse trade.

text.p: German equities ended bourse trade on Wednesday in positive territory, but shy of earlier highs, as the share market pared gains over the session following an early morning recovery.
Market sentiment was hit as the impetus behind the recovery was less dynamic than had been expected.
The DAX index of 30 blue-chip German stocks ended up 5.98 points, or 0.18 percent, at 3,301.91 points, well off a session high of 3,316.73 points. Support at 3,300 points held, however.
"There is still a lot of caution about. The index should settle around 3,300 points over the day," a Frankfurt trader said.
Shares in chemical giant BASF pushed to 61.90 marks in early bourse, but came off over the session to end the day at 61.65 marks, a rise of 65 pfennigs or just over one percent.
Dealers said the market was enthusiastic about the group's 1996 earnings per share (EPS), while the rest of the figures announced earlier were generally in line with expectations.
"The outlook was good. It was cautious, but then we've come to expect that from BASF," a Frankfurt trader.
Positive sentiment in the chemical sector helped lift other stocks. Bayer AG ended up 1.44 percent at 68.68 marks, while Hoechst AG was up 1.10 pfennigs, 1.71 percent, at 65.20 marks.

Dealers said they had expected to see some bargain-hunting over the course of bourse trade, but little ground was gained, the main feeling was one of relief that the market did not lose "Everyone is really just breathing a sigh of relief," a Frankfurt trader said.
